title: Violence and aggression: short-term management in mental health, health and community settings
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
publication: NICE guideline NG10; published 28 May 2015; full update in development
access_status: official recommendations, 2024 surveillance decision, and 2026 update-project status inspected
evidence_scope: Current published UK practice guidance covering developmental assessment, safeguarding, de-escalation, restrictive interventions, debrief, external review, and governance reporting
sequence_allegation: conduct, history, triggers, and immediate harm
sequence_intervention: de-escalation, safeguarding, least-restrictive response, and lawful emergency action

sequence_later_outcome: risk-plan amendment, governing-body reports, and routine outcome monitoring

authors: Monica Gammelgård; Anna-Maija Koivisto; Markku Eronen; Riittakerttu Kaltiala-Heino
access_status: publisher primary record, abstract, DOI, and university publication record inspected
evidence_scope: Record-based short-term predictive validation in 208 adolescents across residential psychiatry, correctional schools, and forensic units
sequence_assessment: SAVRY summary risk assessment from medical and child-welfare records

title: Prospective Field Validation of the START:AV in a Dutch Secure Youth Care Sample
authors: Tamara L. F. De Beuf; Vivienne de Vogel; Nick J. Broers; Corine de Ruiter
access_status: open primary article, tables, appendix, supplement links, DOI, and conflict disclosure inspected
evidence_scope: Preregistered prospective field validation of 106 clinician-completed START:AV assessments with blinded incident coding over four months
sequence_allegation: records, observations, interactions, prior incidents, and professional contacts
sequence_assessment: trained treatment coordinators using the final Dutch START:AV
sequence_review: clinical reassessment context; research interrater and incremental-validity review
sequence_later_outcome: 3,065 coded inpatient incidents across nine outcome categories during four months
notes: Outcome-specific predictive validity was partial; total-score reliability was poor, final judgments added no significant value over lifetime history for tested outcomes, and use was not shown to reduce incidents or liberty restrictions

title: Impact of a debrief tool in acute child and adolescent mental health inpatient units: a centre's experience
authors: William Billal Shepherd; Kyna Patterson; Jessica Blake; Danielle Ward; Ashlee Clarke; Cristina Diaz-Navarro; Farah Abdulsatar
access_status: open primary quality-improvement article and DOI record inspected
evidence_scope: Staff-requested TALK debrief implementation after patient behavioral events with monthly event rate and severity plus informal staff feedback
sequence_review: target, analysis, learning points, actions, delegated follow-up, and care-plan update route
sequence_later_outcome: no significant change in event rate or severity; qualitative staff learning and wellbeing signals
notes: Patients were not involved in study design or debriefs; feedback was informal and unquantified; use was inconsistent during workload surges; the process was neither independent external review nor a test of patient-centered debriefing
